work.abstract_text: For Chakrabarty and Kundu, arXiv:2610.35838v1 (2026), Section III D, page 5, Table III and Eq. (15), we complete the W-state and generalized-GHZ Bell-measurement optimizations and recover the W single-node value from Horodecki et al. (1995). The W-state value is exactly sqrt(13)/3. We prove the upper bound over both central orthonormal frames and every parity-index pair, including identity indices and repeated pairs. A quadratic identity for the W correlation tensor reduces the proof to Parseval's identity and a two-by-two submatrix estimate. Consequently the white-noise threshold in this measurement class is exactly 3/sqrt(13); ignoring either central node gives 2*sqrt(2)/3. An ellipsoid bound gives N_c(GHZ_alpha)=sqrt(1+sin^2(2alpha)), settling the neighboring conjecture. We also give the unequal-visibility threshold and explicit W-state entanglement-swapping probabilities.
